messages.body: stoprule: 'make lint' FAILS on the new command (ruff itself passes: 'uv run ruff check .' -> All checks passed). The Makefile's lint-architecture Check 6 requires every command paired with an sc-*-protocol skill to contain a '## Activation' heading; src/superclaude/commands/spec-panel-stoprule.md has the activation line '> Skill sc:spec-panel-stoprule-protocol' under its title (as the SPEC section 3.1 says) but no '## Activation' heading, so make lint exits 2 ('1 error'). The plan never asked for that heading, and Tasks 9 (variant) and 10 (drift test pinned to the 472-line base) are already complete and reviewed. RECOMMENDED (A): authorize one scoped follow-up before the FINAL review: insert the two lines '## Activation' + blank line directly above the existing '> Skill sc:spec-panel-stoprule-protocol' line, add that heading as one more planned insertion in the drift test's position table, re-run the new tests and make lint, and record it in the ledger as an operator Ruling on Task 9 (cost: the variant gains 2 lines, 481 not 479). (B): change nothing; I report make lint as failing on Check 6 and the coordinator fixes it later. Which?
